methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 106 patients with ampullary carcinoma (2015-2023), with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria, subtype classification by WHO 5th edition with IHC (MUC1, MUC2, CDX2, MUC5AC), and well-defined endpoints. Statistical approach uses Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, univariate and multivariate Cox regression with EPV=5.3 reported (a disciplined choice, but below the conventional 10 threshold as the authors acknowledge). Proportional hazards tested with log-minus-log plots and missing data handled via complete-case analysis. Limitations include single center, retrospective design, small event count, and non-randomized adjuvant therapy analysis; the authors explicitly flag multivariable findings as exploratory.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort without control group classifies as Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is moderate: findings reinforce the importance of R0 resection and multidisciplinary management for this rare malignancy where prospective trials are scarce. The 13.6-month metastatic OS data and exploratory adjusted adjuvant therapy benefit (HR 0.36 for RFS, 0.40 for OS) contribute practical observational evidence, although not practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cohort reporting aligns well with STROBE: clear patient selection, variable definitions, outcome definitions (OS, RFS, PFSmet), statistical methods including EPV disclosure, and transparent acknowledgment of multivariable model limitations. Sensitivity analyses (adjusted adjuvant therapy, subtype-stratified) are reported. Data availability is limited: no deposited dataset, no mention of code sharing, though institutional clinical data typically cannot be shared. REMARK would also be applicable for some prognostic factor elements.

novelty_literature.justification: Ampullary carcinoma prognostic factors (T stage, LVI, PNI, node status, R1 margin, grade) have been extensively studied (Zhang 2022, Luchini 2019 meta-analysis, Buyuktalanci 2025, Vilhordo 2021, all cited). The current study confirms existing findings in a Portuguese cohort and finds R1 margin to be the only independent prognostic factor for RFS. The literature review context is useful but the cohort contribution is primarily confirmatory/incremental.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear tables references, logical flow from demographics through outcomes to prognostic analysis to literature review. Methods and limitations are appropriately transparent. Discussion integrates cohort findings with relevant prior literature without overreach. Minor improvements could be made in condensing the literature review section.

key_strengths: Comprehensive 8-year single-center dataset (n=106) for a rare malignancy with histologically confirmed subtype classification per WHO 5th edition
Transparent disclosure of EPV ratio (5.3) and explicit framing of multivariable findings as exploratory
Contextual literature review integrating findings with meta-analyses and ongoing trials (ADAPTA)
Adjusted analysis suggesting adjuvant therapy benefit (HR 0.36 RFS, 0.40 OS) after accounting for nodal and margin status
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with modest event count limits generalizability
Adjuvant therapy analysis is non-randomized with substantial confounding by indication despite limited covariate adjustment
Findings largely confirm previously reported prognostic factors without identifying novel markers
Histological subtype analysis underpowered (intestinal vs pancreaticobiliary comparisons with small subgroups)
No molecular/genomic profiling despite discussion referencing its growing importance
No data or code sharing statement
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent confirmatory single-center cohort analysis with sound statistical framing and transparent limitations; adds incremental real-world evidence for a rare malignancy but limited novelty places it at Tier 3 with minor revisions.
